newsitem.title: USA: More Latam air cargo alliances seen - consultant.
newsitem.headline: More Latam air cargo alliances seen - consultant.

text.p: More cargo airlines will form alliances focusing on Latin America following the lead of passenger airlines, a prominent airline consultant said here Thursday.
"This will happen as much on the cargo side as on the passenger side," said Robert Booth, president of Aviation Management Services.

Alliances are not new to cargo. A group of Chilean investors that owns cargo carrier Fast Air and passenger carrier LanChile also owns a 24.9 percent stake in Florida West International Airlines. In November, Martinair Holland announced it had bought a 40 percent share of Colombian all-cargo carrier Tampa Airlines S.A.
"Those two are just the tip of the iceburg," Booth said.

It would have been difficult for Fast Air to gain access to U.S. routes from anywhere other than Chile, Booth said. Now the Chilean airline can work with Florida West and have access to these routes such as Colombia-U.S. or Brazil-U.S., he said.
New carriers will also start serving the Miami market, Booth predicted.
